lessons: cycle 15: A high score alone is not sufficient to buy — the cash-target rule binds both directions, blocking a buy when there's nothing clean to deploy just as it blocks idle cash from piling up.

cycle 17: The cash-target band is a percentage, but the funding decision is about absolute dollars — a handful of dollars can sit mid-band and still fund nothing. Once a backlog of 20+/25 candidates goes unfunded for several straight cycles, the backlog itself becomes the binding constraint.

cycle 18: A recurring unfunded backlog can be misdiagnosed as a cash problem when the real constraint is that the book is full (position count over the 8-10 target) — a passing score is necessary but not sufficient with no open slot and no invalidation trigger; decline on construction grounds, don't manufacture an exit.

cycle 19: Even the single best-scoring candidate since the restructure (MDT, 22/25) can't override 'exit when the thesis breaks, not when a better idea comes along' — every current holding sitting at-or-below target weight with an intact thesis means there is no clean lever inside a single cycle's discretion, only an owner call (loosen the band, or a deliberate trim).

cycle 21: An empty fresh-screening pass (both new candidates declined outright) is itself useful information, and doesn't require re-litigating the standing owner decision with the same intensity every time — when there's nothing new, the honest entry is short.

cycle 22: A single-quarter EPS beat sitting on a badly broken multi-month chart (ORCL, RH) fails on trend/quality grounds well before construction even matters — a beat is necessary but nowhere near sufficient. Also: a broad AI-safety-driven selloff hit the untouched watchlist name CAT harder than any held position, since the diversified non-AI sleeve has no direct exposure — mirrors the Cycle 6-7 finding that sector-wide AI sentiment swings aren't by themselves evidence of a company-specific break.

cycle 23: The Cycle 22 AI-safety selloff mostly reversed within days (AI names flat-to-up, CAT's SMA gap narrowed from -8.6% to -4.9%) — confirms holding through narrative-driven selloffs without chasing the recovery either remains correct. Also: two very different-looking new candidates (ADBE, a real earnings beat with cheap headline valuation; ETN, a real AI-power-infrastructure theme) both had a genuine, specific bear case underneath the surface story (a live Goldman Sell rating on ADBE; ETN's price action proving it's MORE correlated to AI-capex sentiment than some held AI names, not less) — a strong headline number or an on-trend narrative isn't sufficient without checking analyst dispersion and actual correlated-theme fit, not just the sector label.

cycle 24: An unprompted analyst upgrade (UBS on UNP, Neutral->Buy) landing on a held laggard with an intact thesis is the payoff for not reflexively trimming/exiting on drawdown alone. Also: a stale analyst mean price target (CMI's, last updated 9/5, implying ~48% upside before checking the date) is not a margin-of-safety signal by itself — always check how recently price targets were set against how much the stock has since moved before treating consensus upside as real.

cycle 25: An EPS beat can still fail on trend when it comes with a revenue miss and a broad same-day wave of analyst price-target cuts (AZO) — the market's reaction to the print matters more than the headline beat/miss framing. Also: LIN's RSI recovering sharply (29.6->43.65) while price stays below its 50-day SMA confirms momentum can lead the moving-average relationship by a wide margin — the SMA-confirmation requirement is deliberately the stricter, later-firing signal, not a redundant one.
cycle 26: A quiet no-trade cycle is fine — a big-name earnings beat (COST) or a cheap yield (PAYX) still fails the score when valuation is rich or the chart is in a long downtrend; keep the bar.

cycles 15-27 / owner review 2026-10-04 (the structural one): 12 consecutive no-trade cycles were NOT a research failure or too high a bar - they were an ARITHMETIC DEADLOCK. Holding 12 single names against an 8-10 band while cash sits at 3.8% inside a 2-5% target means there is zero capacity to act on any new idea without a forced sell, and the agent correctly refuses to sell theses whose invalidation triggers have not fired. Lesson: when 'no trades' repeats for more than ~3 cycles, stop re-screening and audit whether the RULES are blocking action, then say so plainly instead of re-flagging the same backlog.
